name: Your Problem, the Blues
why_it_works: Everyone already sings about their problems in their head. Turning the customer's exact frustration into a slow blues verse makes them laugh and feel seen at once, and the twelve-bar shape promises a resolution, which is where {{brand}} walks in.

hook.pattern: Sing the customer's everyday frustration in a dead-serious blues voice; the mismatch between drama and problem stops the scroll.
examples: We wrote a blues song about {{pain_point}}. Sorry.
If {{pain_point}} had a soundtrack, it would sound like this.

variables.name: pain_point
variables.description: The everyday problem in the customer's words
variables.example: my check-engine light came on again

variables.name: pain_detail
variables.description: A specific, relatable detail that makes it worse
variables.example: and the last shop just shrugged and took my cash

variables.name: fix_line
variables.description: The plain promise of what the business does, true and provable
variables.example: we show you the problem before we fix a thing

beats.purpose: hook: first sung line of the blues

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 photo of a frustrated person in a parked car at dawn, forehead on the steering wheel, cool blue light, moody and cinematic
Vertical slow zoom on a glowing dashboard warning light or a confusing paper bill, shallow focus, blue tint, 9:16
Same person now dramatically singing to the sky, rain on the windshield, blues club lighting gag, vertical
Vertical photo of an empty wallet held upside down, a single coin falling, warm desk lamp light

beats.purpose: resolution: the brand enters, key goes major

visual.prompt: Bright vertical photo inside {{brand}}, smiling staff member handing back keys or paperwork, clean daylight, brand colors, eye-level

slides.headline: The {{pain_point}} blues
slides.body: A song in four verses. Swipe if you've lived it.
slides.visual_prompt: Moody title slide, old blues record label design with the title, deep blue tones

slides.headline: Verse one
slides.visual_prompt: Person staring at the problem in blue morning light, vertical

slides.headline: Verse two
slides.body: I said {{pain_point}}... it's not going away.
slides.visual_prompt: Same person dramatically singing in the rain, film grain

slides.headline: Verse three
slides.visual_prompt: Empty wallet or stack of confusing paperwork on a table, warm lamp

slides.headline: Then the key changes
slides.visual_prompt: Bright, warm photo of the {{brand}} team helping a customer

slides.headline: End the song
slides.visual_prompt: Clean end card with {{brand}} logo and the offer, brand colors

craft.technique: AAB twelve-bar blues verse with major-key resolution
craft.notes: Classic blues shape: line A states the problem, line A repeats it (sung harder, with 'I said' pickup), line B twists it with a worse detail and rhymes with A. Stress the pain word on beat 1 of each bar (WOKE up this MORN-ing). The brand enters on the turnaround and the music shifts from minor/dominant to a bright major chord, so the solution literally sounds like relief. Tempo/feel: 66-72 BPM slow shuffle, triplet swing, slide guitar or harmonica, then a quick drum fill into a brighter final bar.

do_not: Mock the customer; laugh at the problem, not the person
Name or imply a specific real competitor as the 'last shop'
Promise a fix, outcome or price you can't guarantee
compliance: Law firms: no guarantees or implied outcomes ('we'll win your case'); include required attorney-advertising disclaimer and follow your state bar rules
Insurance and mortgage: no promised rates, approvals or savings amounts; include license number (NMLS for mortgage) and 'terms and eligibility apply'
Dental: do not guarantee pain-free or specific results; pain points must not reveal any real patient's information
